title: Anaphylaxis Management
description: Immediate management of anaphylactic reaction. Time-critical — epinephrine first.

steps.text: Suspect anaphylaxis? (urticaria + hypotension/bronchospasm/laryngeal edema after trigger)
EPINEPHRINE 0.3 mg (0.3 mL of 1:1000) IM into outer thigh. Repeat q5–10 min if no improvement.
steps.note: Do NOT delay — epinephrine is first-line. Antihistamines/steroids are adjuncts, NOT substitutes.

steps.text: Call emergency services (112/911). Lay patient flat, legs elevated. If unconscious + no pulse: start CPR.
Response to epinephrine?
Monitor 4–8h (biphasic reaction risk). IV access. O2 by mask. Consider: methylprednisolone 125mg IV, diphenhydramine 25–50mg IV.
REFRACTORY: Epinephrine infusion 0.1–1 mcg/kg/min IV. Vasopressors. Intubate if airway threatened. ICU transfer.
Discharge criteria (after ≥4h obs, no symptoms): prescribe EpiPen × 2, allergy referral, anaphylaxis action plan.

title: Hypoglycemia Management
description: Acute management of blood glucose <70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L).
source: ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2024

steps.text: Blood glucose <70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) OR symptomatic hypoglycemia?
Patient conscious and able to swallow?
RULE OF 15: Give 15g fast-acting carbs (4 glucose tabs, 150mL juice, 150mL regular soda). Wait 15 min, recheck BG.
BG still <70 after 15 min?
UNCONSCIOUS/UNABLE TO SWALLOW: Glucagon 1mg IM/SC (or nasal glucagon 3mg). If no IV — use glucagon. Call EMS.
IV access available: 50% Dextrose 50mL IV bolus (D50W). Repeat if no improvement in 5 min.
Maintain: D10W infusion to keep BG 100–180. Monitor q30 min until stable ×2h.
Once stable: eat full meal. Review insulin dose, timing, diet. Adjust if recurrent. Educate on hypoglycemia prevention.
Severe (BG <40 or loss of consciousness): hospitalize, investigate cause (insulin dose error, infection, adrenal insufficiency).

title: Cardiac Arrest — BLS Algorithm
description: Basic Life Support algorithm for adult cardiac arrest (ILCOR 2020).

steps.text: Unresponsive + not breathing normally?
CALL EMS (112/911). Get AED. Note time of collapse.
START CPR: 30 compressions (5–6 cm depth, 100–120/min) + 2 rescue breaths. Minimise interruptions (<10 sec).
AED arrived?
Power on AED → place pads (right clavicle, left flank) → analyse rhythm.
Shockable rhythm (VF/pVT)?
SHOCK: Clear patient → deliver shock → immediately resume 5 cycles CPR (2 min) → reanalyse.
After ROSC: place in recovery position, O2 12–15 L/min, IV access, vitals q5 min. Transfer to ACLS-capable facility.
Non-shockable (PEA/Asystole): Continue CPR 2 min, treat reversible causes (4H4T: hypoxia, hypovolemia, hypothermia, H+ [acidosis]; tension pneumo, tamponade, thrombosis, toxins).

title: Acute Ischemic Stroke — FAST + tPA Decision
description: Acute stroke recognition and IV thrombolysis eligibility assessment.

steps.text: Sudden onset: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty? → FAST positive? → Activate stroke team.
Time is brain: door-to-CT goal <25 min. NPO, IV access, O2 if SpO2 <94%, glucose check, 12-lead ECG.
NIHSS score. Non-contrast CT head — rule out hemorrhage. CT angio if large vessel occlusion suspected.
Hemorrhage on CT?
Within 4.5h of symptom onset AND no contraindications to IV tPA?
IV ALTEPLASE 0.9 mg/kg (max 90mg): 10% bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 min. No anticoagulants/antiplatelets for 24h. ICU monitoring.
Consider mechanical thrombectomy if LVO on CTA + NIHSS ≥6 + within 24h (selected patients up to 24h with perfusion imaging).
Door-to-needle goal: <60 min. BP management: maintain <185/110 before tPA; <180/105 during/after. Admit stroke unit.
HEMORRHAGIC STROKE: Neurosurgery consult. BP control (target <140 systolic), reverse anticoagulation if applicable, ICU.

title: Sepsis — Screening & Initial Management
description: qSOFA screening + Sepsis-3 management bundle (1-hour bundle).

steps.text: Suspected infection + ≥2 qSOFA criteria? (RR ≥22, altered mentation, SBP ≤100)
steps.note: qSOFA is a rapid bedside screen — not diagnostic.

steps.text: FULL ASSESSMENT: SOFA score, lactate, blood cultures ×2 (before antibiotics if feasible <45 min delay).
Septic Shock? (MAP <65 despite fluids, Lactate >2 mmol/L)
1-HOUR BUNDLE: Blood cultures → Broad-spectrum antibiotics (within 1h) → 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid if hypotensive or lactate ≥4 → Measure lactate.
ANTIBIOTICS: Choose based on suspected source (e.g., piperacillin/tazobactam + vancomycin for unknown source). De-escalate per culture results.
SEPTIC SHOCK: Norepinephrine (vasopressor of choice, target MAP ≥65). IV hydrocortisone 200mg/day if refractory. ICU transfer.
Source control within 6–12h (e.g., drain abscess, remove infected catheter). Procalcitonin-guided antibiotic duration. Daily reassessment.

title: Hypertensive Emergency vs Urgency
description: Differentiation and management of severe hypertension with/without end-organ damage.

steps.text: BP >180/120 mmHg?
Assess for end-organ damage: chest pain (ACS/dissection), dyspnea/rales (HF), headache+vision changes (encephalopathy), focal neurology (stroke), oliguria (AKI).
Evidence of end-organ damage?
EMERGENCY: IV antihypertensives. Target: reduce MAP by ≤25% in 1h, then to 160/100 over next 2–6h. ICU admission.
IV options: Labetalol 20mg IV q10min (avoid in HF/asthma), Nicardipine 5mg/h infusion, Sodium nitroprusside (for encephalopathy/dissection), Esmolol (for dissection).
AORTIC DISSECTION: Target SBP 100–120 + HR <60. Esmolol + Nicardipine. Urgent CT angio → Surgery for Type A.
URGENCY (no end-organ damage): Oral antihypertensives (captopril 25mg, amlodipine, labetalol). Lower BP over 24–48h. Outpatient follow-up. Do NOT treat too aggressively.
Recheck BP after 30 min of oral meds. If no response or new symptoms → reassess as Emergency. Avoid sublingual nifedipine (rapid drop risk).

title: Acute Asthma Exacerbation
description: Emergency assessment and stepwise management of acute asthma attack.
source: GINA Global Strategy for Asthma Management 2024

steps.text: Dyspnea, wheeze, chest tightness? Assess severity: SpO2, speech, RR, HR, accessory muscles, PEFR.
Severity?
MILD-MODERATE: SABA (albuterol) 4–8 puffs MDI q20 min × 3 in 1h (or 2.5mg nebulized). Add ipratropium 4 puffs.
Systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 40–50mg oral or methylprednisolone 125mg IV). O2 titrated to SpO2 94–98%.
Response after 1h (PEFR >70%, SpO2 ≥94%)?
SEVERE: Continuous SABA nebs + ipratropium. IV corticosteroids. O2 high-flow. IV Mg sulfate 2g over 20 min (reduces hospitalization).
LIFE-THREATENING (silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered consciousness): Intubation, ICU. Avoid ketamine caution in tachycardic patients.
Consider IV aminophylline if no response to above (elderly/severe): loading 5mg/kg over 20 min (if not on theophylline), then 0.5mg/kg/h.
Discharge: PEFR >70% predicted, SpO2 ≥94% on room air, symptoms well-controlled. Prescribe: ICS, SABA rescue, written action plan. Review in 2 days.

title: Chest Pain — Emergency Triage
description: Rapid systematic approach to acute chest pain in the ED.
source: ESC Acute Chest Pain Guidelines 2023; AHA NSTEMI Guidelines 2023

steps.text: Acute chest pain. IMMEDIATE: 12-lead ECG within 10 min of presentation. IV access, O2 if SpO2 <90%, vitals.
ST elevation on ECG? (≥1mm in ≥2 contiguous leads, or new LBBB)
STEMI: Activate cathlab NOW. Aspirin 300mg + P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor 180mg). Target: primary PCI within 90 min of first medical contact.
If PCI not available within 120 min: fibrinolysis (tenecteplase/alteplase) if no contraindications.
NON-STEMI/UNSTABLE ANGINA: hs-Troponin at presentation + 1h (or 3h). Risk stratify with GRACE/TIMI score.
Troponin elevated (above 99th percentile)?
NSTEMI: Anticoagulation (fondaparinux 2.5mg SC or enoxaparin). Aspirin + P2Y12. Early invasive strategy if high-risk (GRACE >140, refractory ischemia).
If troponin negative × 2: consider other diagnoses (PE — Wells score, aortic dissection — D-dimer/CT, pericarditis, GERD, MSK).
ALL ACS: Dual antiplatelet therapy, beta-blocker (if no contraindication), high-intensity statin. Cardiology follow-up. ECHO before discharge.

title: Status Epilepticus Management
description: Time-based algorithm for adult convulsive status epilepticus.
source: Neurocritical Care Society Guidelines 2023; EAN Guidelines 2023

steps.text: Seizure >5 min OR ≥2 seizures without return to baseline? → Status epilepticus. Start clock. ABC: airway, O2, IV access, glucose check.
PHASE 1 (0–5 min): IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4mg, repeat once if no IV: IM midazolam 10mg or rectal diazepam 10mg).
Seizure stopped after benzodiazepine?
PHASE 2 (10–20 min): Choose ONE: IV levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4.5g) over 10 min; OR IV valproate 40 mg/kg over 10 min; OR IV phenytoin 20 mg/kg over 20 min.
Seizure stopped?
REFRACTORY (>30 min): ICU, intubation, EEG monitoring. IV propofol 1–2 mg/kg bolus then 2–10 mg/kg/h; OR midazolam infusion 0.05–0.4 mg/kg/h; OR IV phenobarbital 20 mg/kg.
SUPER-REFRACTORY (>24h): Consider ketamine, isoflurane (general anesthesia), ketogenic diet, immunotherapy (if autoimmune cause suspected).
Post-ictal care: Find and treat cause (hyponatremia, meningitis, hypoglycemia, toxic, structural). Brain MRI, LP if meningitis suspected. AED continuation.

title: Acute Toxin Ingestion — Dogs & Cats
description: Emergency management of common household toxin ingestion in small animals.
source: Merck Veterinary Manual 2023; ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center

steps.text: Known or suspected toxin ingestion in dog or cat? Identify toxin + time of ingestion + amount (if known).
Call APCC (888-426-4435) or local vet emergency. Stabilize ABCs: airway, breathing, circulation. IV access.
Ingestion within 1–2 hours + patient conscious + no seizures/aspiration risk?
EMESIS (dogs only, NOT cats with most protocols): 3% H₂O₂ 2.2 mL/kg PO (max 45 mL). OR apomorphine 0.04 mg/kg IV. Wait 15 min. Never induce emesis for caustics, hydrocarbons, or unconscious animals.
ACTIVATED CHARCOAL (if appropriate toxin, within 4h): 1–4 g/kg PO with cathartic (sorbitol). Not for ethanol, heavy metals, corrosives.
Specific toxin antidote available?
ANTIDOTES: Xylitol/hypoglycemia → dextrose IV; Acetaminophen (cats) → N-acetylcysteine; Rodenticide (anticoag) → Vitamin K1; Opioids → Naloxone; Organophosphates → Atropine + pralidoxime.
SUPPORTIVE CARE: Control seizures (diazepam), treat hyperthermia (cooling), IV fluids for hypotension, monitor ECG/urine output, liver/kidney panels q4h.
Common toxins: Xylitol (dogs, severe hypoglycemia + hepatotoxic), grapes/raisins (renal failure dogs), NSAIDs (GI/renal), chocolate (theobromine, tachyarrhythmia), metaldehyde (slugs, seizures).
